Select T\'Eyes developer options restorer in the Accessibility list, then enable its service.
Open Android Settings → Accessibility manually, then select T\'Eyes developer options restorer.

Enable T\'Eyes developer options restorer in Accessibility Settings first.\n\nIf Android blocks it, open App Info, tap the top-right three-dot menu and allow restricted settings. Then return to Accessibility Settings and enable the service.
Open Android Settings → Apps → T\'Eyes developer options restorer manually.

The native Quick Settings panel was requested. Tap the Wireless debugging tile and accept the confirmation.\n\nIf the tile is missing, add it from Developer Options → Quick settings developer tiles. Opening the panel does not enable Wireless debugging automatically.
Android did not accept the request to open Quick Settings. Check that the accessibility service is enabled, then try again.

1. Disable automatic date and time. Set the date to November 11, 2019, and the time to 11:11 AM.

2. Go to System Settings → System → Default Settings and enter 502105. Do not change any of the switches that appear.

3. While the time is still 11:11 AM, go to Android Settings → About and tap Build Number seven times to enable Developer Options.

4. Install T'Eyes developer options restorer.

5. Open Android Settings → Accessibility and select T'Eyes developer options restorer. Try to enable the service. If Android blocks it, continue with the next step.

6. Go to Android Settings → Apps → T'Eyes developer options restorer. Tap the small three-dot menu in the top-right corner and allow restricted settings. Do not confuse this with the split-screen button on the navigation bar.

7. Return to Accessibility and enable the service for T'Eyes developer options restorer.

8. Go to Developer Options → Quick settings developer tiles and enable the Wireless debugging tile.

9. Open T'Eyes developer options restorer. Tap the hamburger menu in the top-right corner and choose Open Android Quick Settings.

10. The native Android Quick Settings panel will open. Tap Wireless debugging to enable it.

11. Connect from the same Wi-Fi network to the head unit's IP address, for example 192.168.x.x:7575. Use port 7575, not 5555. Confirm the debugging permission in the popup on the head unit.

12. Set the date and time back to automatic.
